sentence_as_it_stands: Good: wheals of plain lidocaine made from these ampoules by the dilution the one wheal study in a neuropathic condition describes are the form that study used, and it reported improvement without a control group.

page: Relief that outlasts the block — and whether the whole list is optimising the wrong thing
sentence_as_it_stands: Every series is in neuralgia after nerve injury, phantom limb pain, vulvodynia, back pain or myofascial pain.
quote: In the current study, 20 patients in the NP group suffering from pruritus and neuropathic pain were locally administered therapeutic lidocaine, and improvement was observed to sustain for up to 3 months.
corrected_wording: Every series found is in neuralgia after nerve injury, phantom limb pain, vulvodynia, back pain or myofascial pain, apart from one uncontrolled series of intradermal lidocaine papules in notalgia paresthetica, a sensory neuropathy of the upper back, with pain and itch lower at three months and no documented skin numbness (Mülkoğlu 2020, PMID 32416719); none is in small fibre neuropathy.
notes: The page does not cite Mülkoğlu 2020 anywhere (0 hits for Mülkoğlu/Mulkoglu/notalgia/32416719), though it is the published series closest to the reader's route (repeated intradermal papules) and class of condition, on the page's own question. Not a tested claim (the sentence is the first half of the bullet whose second half is D030). Rated low as wording too narrow; the main session may weigh it higher given its relevance. (Not from this paper: postherpetic-neuralgia infiltration series such as Rowbotham 1989 also fall outside the list.)

section: 12.3a Protocol design from the closest existing intervention
sentence_as_it_stands: One wheal protocol with a local anaesthetic and a pain outcome has been published: [dose figure omitted] of [dose figure omitted] lidocaine diluted in [dose figure omitted] of saline, [dose figure omitted] wheals [dose figure omitted] apart, [dose figure omitted], with pain lower at 2 and 4 weeks and at 3 months in 20 people with notalgia paresthetica, uncontrolled, and none in small fibre neuropathy (Mülkoğlu 2020, PMID 32416719).
quote: We also previously reported a 73-year-old male case with NP treated with therapeutic lidocaine injections. In that case, we locally administered lidocaine into the upper back to relieve pain and obtained successful results related to neuropathic back pain.
corrected_wording: One wheal series with a local anaesthetic, its parameters stated and a pain outcome in a neuropathic condition has been found: pain lower at 2 and 4 weeks and at 3 months in 20 people with notalgia paresthetica, uncontrolled (Mülkoğlu 2020, PMID 32416719); the same authors earlier reported a single case treated with local lidocaine injections (Mülkoğlu 2018, PMID 29911324); none is in small fibre neuropathy.
notes: Every methods, schedule, n and outcome detail of the sentence matches p3–5 and Table 3 (checked; not reproduced). Only the opening clause overreaches, by dropping the qualifiers that section 13 keeps ('What has been reported only once is an anaesthetic-only wheal protocol with per-wheal volume, spacing, a repeated-session schedule and a pain outcome …', which this paper does not contradict). Ambiguous because the 2020 text does not give the 2018 case's route. Other published wheal studies with a pain outcome that the record already holds (the Colombian procaine papule trial on the Relief page; Loughnan 2009 in D029) also bear on this clause but are not from this paper. S1 is testing this page.

section: Where procaine sits against the other candidates (repeated in The recommendation)
sentence_as_it_stands: If the object is relief that outlasts the block, procaine is the drug the literature actually uses, and its shortness is not a defect. The published infiltration series are procaine series: [dose figure omitted] procaine at [dose figure omitted] a session ([dose figure omitted]) over [dose figure omitted] in 45 women with severe chronic vulvodynia — 36 of 45 responding ([dose figure omitted]), pain 7.9 → 2.4 on the 0–10 scale (P < .001), benefit in responders lasting 6.8 to 125 months, median 24.1 months, and no adverse events. A second series of 280 referred refractory chronic-pain patients treated with procaine or lidocaine alone, [dose figure omitted], reports [dose figure omitted] needing less analgesia or none at one year. Neither is controlled, neither is a neuropathy cohort, …
quote: In the current study, 20 patients in the NP group suffering from pruritus and neuropathic pain were locally administered therapeutic lidocaine, and improvement was observed to sustain for up to 3 months.
corrected_wording: If the object is relief that outlasts the block, the published uncontrolled infiltration series used procaine (vulvodynia, 45 women), procaine or lidocaine (280 refractory chronic-pain patients, Egli 2015) and lidocaine (intradermal papules in notalgia paresthetica, a sensory neuropathy, with pain and itch lower at three months; Mülkoğlu 2020, PMID 32416719); none is controlled.
notes: The page's Recommendation repeats the point: '… and, if the relief that outlasts a block is real, procaine is the drug that literature actually uses.' The section's own second series was procaine or lidocaine, and the notalgia series (lidocaine) is a neuropathy cohort, against 'Neither is … a neuropathy cohort'. The page does not cite Mülkoğlu 2020. Not a tested claim (grep for 'procaine series', 'literature actually uses': 0 claims). Medium because the page's recommendation leans on it; the recommendation's main ground (resting a site) is untouched.

section: What is still unknown (Whether procaine's short block matters at all)
sentence_as_it_stands: The uncontrolled series that report months of benefit used the shortest-acting drug in the group and did not compare it against any other.
quote: The relief of pain and pruritus continued for up to 3 months.
corrected_wording: The uncontrolled series that report months of benefit used procaine, procaine or lidocaine, or lidocaine alone (Mülkoğlu 2020, notalgia paresthetica, PMID 32416719), and none compared one anaesthetic against another.
notes: Mülkoğlu 2020 is an uncontrolled series reporting pain and itch lower to three months with lidocaine, not procaine; like the others it compared no anaesthetics. Same root as F06.

page: 2 — Reference — Topical Treatments for Small Fiber Neuropathy
section: 4.9 · Injected local anaesthetics — the current regimen (header line)
sentence_as_it_stands: Magnitude UNKNOWN by this route in this condition · Duration published for procaine and lidocaine in other neuropathic conditions, median 24.1 months in the largest series · Evidence NONE in small fibre neuropathy; two randomised trials in adjacent conditions
quote: Treatment success was measured after one year follow-up using the outcome measures of pain and analgesics intake.
corrected_wording: Duration published for procaine in a chronic pelvic pain series (median 24.1 months among responders, 45 women) and for lidocaine in notalgia paresthetica (pain and itch lower to three months, 20 people; Mülkoğlu 2020, PMID 32416719); the largest series (280 patients given procaine or lidocaine; Egli 2015, PMID 26115657) reports status at one year rather than a duration.
notes: The 24.1-month median belongs to the 45-woman vulvodynia series (tagged S174 in the same section), which the register's own S174 entry calls 'a chronic pelvic pain one and not a neuropathy one'. The largest series in the section, Egli 2015 (280; Mülkoğlu's ref 29, found through its reference list), measured outcomes at one year and gives no median duration; the section's 127-patient mepivacaine series is also larger than 45. The one neuropathic-condition duration in the section is this paper's (to three months).

page: What is still unsettled across these pages, and what would settle each one
section: Which primary sources are unread, and what each would settle — Full text of J Anesth Clin Res 2012;3(3):199
sentence_as_it_stands: The paper is paywalled and its eight primary references are the closest thing that exists to evidence for repeated intradermal wheals as a technique in use.
quote: In this study, we intradermally administered lidocaine diluted with saline into the upper back over [dose figure omitted].
corrected_wording: The paper is closed access and its eight primary references, which required a demonstrated anaesthetic effect on the skin, are unread; a published series of repeated intradermal lidocaine papules with its schedule stated exists in notalgia paresthetica (Mülkoğlu 2020, PMID 32416719, free in PMC; uncontrolled; no documented skin numbness).
notes: The page's opening summary repeats it: 'A second paywalled paper's reference list is the closest thing that exists to evidence for repeated intradermal wheals as a technique'. Vlassakov's abstract (OpenAlex W2332856010) describes outcomes 'With the single skin anesthesia treatment', so the eight may not concern repeated wheals at all; this paper does. The open question itself (what the eight papers are) is not answered: the full text was closed access and not reachable here either (doi.org and Crossref blocked by the session's network policy; the Jina reader returned HTTP 401).

page: Relief that outlasts the block — and whether the whole list is optimising the wrong thing
section: What is still unknown (What is in the eight papers)
sentence_as_it_stands: *What would settle it:* the full text of *J Anesth Clin Res* 2012;3(3):199 and its reference list — those eight primary papers are the closest thing that exists to evidence for what he is doing.
quote: In this study, we intradermally administered lidocaine diluted with saline into the upper back over [dose figure omitted].
corrected_wording: What would settle it: the full text of J Anesth Clin Res 2012;3(3):199 and its reference list — those eight primary papers are the closest evidence on cutaneous anaesthesia with documented numbness in neuropathic pain; the closest published report of the route itself, repeated intradermal lidocaine papules in a sensory neuropathy, is an uncontrolled series in notalgia paresthetica that did not document numbness (Mülkoğlu 2020, PMID 32416719).
notes: Same point as the claim update on D032 (its also-text 'the closest paper in existence to what this reader is doing', in other sections of this page) and as F11; recorded because it adds this location. The judgement trades demonstrated numbness (the eight) against route, repetition and stated schedule (this paper); hence low.
